title: Maximize the Beauty of the Garden
description:
There is a garden of `n` flowers, and each flower has an integer beauty value. The flowers are arranged in a line. You are given an integer array `flowers` of size `n` and each `flowers[i]` represents the beauty of the `i^th` flower.

A garden is **valid** if it meets these conditions:

	The garden has at least two flowers.
	The first and the last flower of the garden have the same beauty value.

As the appointed gardener, you have the ability to **remove** any (possibly none) flowers from the garden. You want to remove flowers in a way that makes the remaining garden **valid**. The beauty of the garden is the sum of the beauty of all the remaining flowers.

Return the maximum possible beauty of some **valid** garden after you have removed any (possibly none) flowers.

examples.explanation: You can produce the valid garden [2,3,1,2] to have a total beauty of 2 + 3 + 1 + 2 = 8.
You can produce the valid garden [1,1,1] to have a total beauty of 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.
You can produce the valid garden [-1,-1] to have a total beauty of -1 + -1 = -2.

constraints: It is possible to create a valid garden by removing some (possibly none) flowers.
hints: Analyze the constraints and data structures appropriate for Maximize the Beauty of the Garden.
Formulate an optimal state transition or traversal invariant.
Consider corner testcases and boundary limits.
